notes:
Account snapshot and user notes:
- Vertical: autonomy stack for medium/long haul industrial vehicles. Heavy telemetry, multi-modal upstream, and safety-critical routing decisions.
- Primary ask: Dedicated pool with guaranteed throughput and clear latency SLOs for both chat-style assist and high-rate reranking pipelines.
- Performance targets (customer stated): p50 token latency <50ms for short prompts; p95 end-to-end response <350ms for 256-token completions in chat; reranking pipelines require 1,000 qps (batching ok) with p95 end-to-end <150ms for single-turn short prompts.
- Capacity sizing ask: reserve GPUs to handle sustained 1,000 qps reranking plus bursts to 2,500 qps for peak routes. Expect ~12-18 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (customer provided rough ops calc). Looking for Redwood to vet kernel/quantization gains to reduce GPU count.
- POC approach agreed: 3-stage bench: (1) baseline throughput run w/ synthetic traffic + representative prompts, (2) cold-start soak (72h) with telemetry to catch memory leaks/KV cache pressure, (3) failure/fallback test (simulate node loss & automatic fallback to lower-capacity model variant).
- Representative prompt sets uploaded to drive: long-context incident logs (avg 6k tokens), short telemetry snippets for reranking (10-60 tokens), multi-turn dialogue for remote operator assist (avg 200 tokens).
- Observability asks: token-level cost breakdown, per-route p95/p99, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization heatmap. They want these surfaced in Console and in a weekly export CSV.
- Security: must pass KMS integration test and provide proof of audit_logging behaviour and retention controls. Data residency requirement: customer data must remain in us-east-1 for POC and production.
- Quote from procurement on kickoff: "We need deterministic throughput guarantees — anything less and we cannot put safety-critical routing on it."
- Pricing sensitivity: willing to commit to annual reserved capacity if Redwood can offer firm throughput SLAs and a cost-per-concurrent-session cap.
- Notable risks: our fallback model introduces 8-12% latency improvement but ~2-3% gen-quality regressions; they require eval harness to quantify safety/quality delta.
- Internal notes: SE to run additional microbench for long-context transformer compilation flags (flash attention variants) to see if p95 improves for 6k token windows.
- Next immediate deliverable: Dedicated soak test final report (metrics + recommended reserved GPU plan) and SLA draft with clear remediation credits on missed throughput.
- Suggested meeting cadence: twice-weekly sync during soak (Mon/Thu) then weekly once stable.
